## Problem

TorchServe is the model server where the unauthenticated-surface class
became an executable class. Management actions — register a model,
delete a model, change its default version — ride a second port
(:8081, management) whose default bind is loopback, but whose
register-and-download shape is the dangerous one: with `allowed_urls`
config set broadly, the `POST /models` request takes a `url`
parameter pointing at a `.mar` archive that the server will fetch,
and the archive carries the handler — a Python module executed inside
the server. That RCE class is not hypothetical: CVE-2023-43654
(CVSS 10.0) is exactly the remote-archive → registration → RCE chain
(fixed 0.8.2), CVE-2023-48299 the upload ZipSlip (fixed 0.9.0), and
CVE-2024-35198 the `..`-bypass of `allowed_urls` (fixed 0.11.0), with
CVE-2024-35199 exposing the gRPC management/inference plane on all
interfaces (fixed 0.11.0). Upstream's own banner says the maintenance
story out loud: "Limited Maintenance — no planned security patches".
The manifest maps the surface to OWASP LLM02 + LLM10 and the
`torchserve-pwn` row to ATLAS AML.T0049 + T0050. You want a
reproducible audit that maps the surface, proves WHICH flag closes
each leg, and never fires a transcript-grade payload.

## Solution

This is an audit recipe, not a transcript recipe: the probe leg shows
the management surface's request shape and which flag closes it — no
payload firing, no invented transcript:

```bash
# 1. BOOT THE LAB TARGET (isolated lab segment):
#      kailash info torchserve
#    -> defaults 127.0.0.1:8080 (inference) / 127.0.0.1:8081
#       (management) / 127.0.0.1:8082 (metrics), gRPC 7070/7071.
#    Exposed leg = management port reachable from the segment AND the
#    two deliberate lab acts: TS_DISABLE_TOKEN_AUTHORIZATION set (or
#    --disable-token-auth passed — token auth is ON by default) and
#    --enable-model-api passed (model register/delete are DISABLED by
#    default). Both acts belong in the lab only — see [Gate lab-mode
#    and exp-classified tools](../admin/lab-mode-gating.html) for how
#    exp A-7 rows reach a lab.

# 2. FIRST GATE CHECK — token auth, the default-on gate:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://<target>:8081/models
#    -> 401 (token-gated management API, the module default)
#    the token rides the request as X-Api-Key; fetch it the way
#    torchserve writes it at boot (key file path per your launch).

# 3. THE SHAPE (management register — the RCE class, NOT executed):
#    With token auth disabled AND --enable-model-api passed (register/
#    delete are disabled by default — the flag is what opens them),
#    the register shape is:
curl -fsS -X POST 'http://<target>:8081/models?url=<mar-url>&handler=<handler>&batchSize=1'
#    url=     the .mar archive the SERVER will fetch (with allowed_urls
#             set broadly — the CVE-2023-43654 / -35198 class)
#    handler= the handler entry-point INSIDE that archive; it is a
#             Python module executed by the server = the deserialization
#             class
#    -> the probe demonstrates the SHAPE; firing it (a real crafted
#       .mar at a real allowed_urls) is outside the audit's need and
#       outside the responsible-use line. The shape itself + which
#       flags close it IS the finding.

# 4. THE CLOSING MAP (each leg → its flag):
#      leg "management reachable at all"
#        -> keep management bound to loopback (the default bind) —
#           the segment must not see :8081; the gRPC plane's own CVE
#           (all-interfaces exposure) wants the same answer: loopback
#           or firewall.
#      leg "token auth"  -> DEFAULT ON. Keep it on: the audit's
#           closed-state proof is that TS_DISABLE_TOKEN_AUTHORIZATION
#           stays UNSET and --disable-token-auth is never passed.
#      leg "model register/delete API"
#           -> register/delete are DISABLED BY DEFAULT; keep the
#              default: --enable-model-api is never passed in
#              production (flag-off closes the register/delete verbs
#              at the server), which closes leg #3 outright.

# 5. THE FLIP + SAME PROBES:
#      restart the target at the hardened posture: token auth ON
#      (the default), --enable-model-api NOT passed (the default),
#      management bound to loopback (the default bind):
sudo nixos-rebuild test      # or relaunch the container with defaults
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://<target>:8081/models
#    -> keyless probe FAILs with 401 under default token auth
#       (vs ok in the exposed leg). Diff = evidence.
```

Expected output shape (abridged, shapes not transcripts):

```
sweep @ <target>  posture: exposed leg (token auth disabled,
                            --enable-model-api passed, mgmt reachable)
  :8081/models (keyless) -> 401 with token auth ON (default posture),
                            keyless-OK only when token auth disabled
  :8081 register shape   -> shape demonstrated; flags that close it:
                            token auth (default ON) + --enable-model-api
                            off + management loopback bind + allowed_urls
                            tightened (no broad wildcard, no .mar fetch
                            from arbitrary urls — the CVE class)
  inference plane        -> :8080 /predictions/{model} (keyless-OK only
                            under the same disabled-token posture)
sweep again, hardened posture (defaults + loopback mgmt)
  keyless management probe -> FAIL 401/403 — surface closed
```

## Discussion

- **Why the shape without a transcript:** the RCE chain (remote `.mar`
  fetch → handler execution) is a real exploit technique with real
  CVEs behind it; a cookbook transcript of a fired payload is a
  public exploit walkthrough, while the audit form — shape, flag map,
  posture flip — is the defensible lab discipline. The A-7 discipline
  across this book (see [Attack the platform, then
  verify](attack-then-verify.html)) exists exactly for surfaces of
  this class: no invented transcript, verdict discipline, diff as
  evidence.
- **The CVE map with fix versions (the audit's backbone):**
  - **CVE-2023-43654 (CVSS 10.0, fixed 0.8.2):** the
    `allowed_urls` → remote `.mar` download → registration RCE chain
    — the reason this recipe is Level hard.
  - **CVE-2023-48299 (fixed 0.9.0):** ZipSlip traversal on archive
    upload — path escape via crafted archive entries.
  - **CVE-2024-35198 (fixed 0.11.0):** `..`-bypass of `allowed_urls`
    restrictions — the allowlist that closes 43654 leaks via
    traversal.
  - **CVE-2024-35199 (fixed 0.11.0):** gRPC plane on all interfaces —
    the "one bind mistake" analog for the 7070/7071 listeners.
  All four resolve to the same closing map as the flags above: bind
  discipline, auth ON, model-API off, allowed_urls tightened, and a
  version at/after the fixes — check `torchserve --version` and your
  pin against the list.
- **Why the version check is part of the flip:** TorchServe is in
  "Limited Maintenance — no planned security patches" (upstream
  banner), which means waiting for the NEXT fix is not a plan; the
  closing map must carry the load. A pin at/after 0.11.0 closes the
  four CVEs above; the operational flags + binds close the CLASS. The
  manifest carries torchserve as an O-2 row (lab target), so the
  audit leg is the recipe's honest shape: demonstrate exposure in a
  controlled lab, close it by configuration, and diff the sweeps.
- **The observability defence leg is a pending row, stated honestly:**
  Langfuse is the trace destination the manifest owns for LLM
  telemetry: OTel endpoint `/api/public/otel`,
  `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` carrying `Basic <pk-lf-…>:<sk-lf-…>`,
  plus the `x-langfuse-ingestion-version: 4` header, self-host via
  docker-compose. The kailash-langfuse module row is pending/unwired
  at the pin (PENDING) — the upstream export shape is quoted as the
  design. What the traces would give the operator: standing
  visibility of management-API calls (register/delete) and inference
  volume — the anomaly view the probe sweep hand-verified.
- **Why plain probes and not a bespoke exploit script:** `torchserve-pwn`
  is an A-7 row, `safety.level: exp`, licence `LicenseRef-Unknown`,
  upstream repository missing at the pin
  ([kailash-os#23](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/23)).
  The real tool takes over via the double-key lab gate when its
  derivation lands (walk: [Gate lab-mode and exp-classified
  tools](../admin/lab-mode-gating.html)); the probe leg runs with
  base-system curl.
- **This is the transferable pattern** (lab target up → shape
  audits → posture flip → same probes → diff). Origin walk:
  [Attack the platform, then verify](attack-then-verify.html).
